extracted.intended_audience: young mathematicians, prospective contributors and subscribers to The Mathematician (mid-19th-century mathematical periodical)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial policy and author guidance for submissions to the nineteenth-century periodical 'The Mathematician': what kinds of mathematical questions, papers, methods, and expositions will be accepted and encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection — only substantive/new-principle questions
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘‘We shall, hence, insert only such as involve some new principle, or require for their solution some new modes of investigation,—such as either lead to results remarkable for their unexpected simplicity, elegance, and symmetry; or tend to the extension of an old, or to the commencement of a new, and valuable course of inquiry.’’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude routine problems that lead to petty calculation; preference for problems that introduce new principles, require new methods, yield elegant/simple/symmetric results, extend an existing line of inquiry, or begin a valuable new one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid trivial exercises / do not encourage mere problem-solvers
rubrics_metrics.description: The department of mathematical questions will be curtailed because 'the insertion of such as lead to mere petty details of calculation and deduction, suited only for the student’s private exercise, tends not only to lead him into frivolous researches, but to create a false taste in science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject or deprioritize submissions whose chief value is routine calculation practice; the journal seeks to avoid 'creating a race of mere problem-solvers.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical model and exposition quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editors intend 'to furnish good models for the young student’s imitation in conducting his own researches, and in putting them into a finished form.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should present clear, simplified investigations and polished exposition suitable as examples for students — i.e., well-presented finished papers rather than rough notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplification and efficiency of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: One feature will be the attempt 'to simplify both the investigations and modes of actual operation of various elementary processes' and 'by reducing to simple and symmetrical processes several of the operations of arithmetic and algebra, to diminish the inevitable labours of calculation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer methods that simplify operations, reduce computational labour, or present more elegant/efficient procedures (practical interest in Horner-type simplifications is cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — modern geometry and Continental methods
rubrics_metrics.description: A third object will be 'to develop in sufficient detail those methods in geometry, which have been devised and carried out to considerable extent by the Continental Mathematicians' (Modern Geometry, Descriptive Geometry, Method of Poles, Geometry of the Rule, Method of Projections, Anharmonic Ratio, Transversals, spherical coordinates, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers treating, illustrating, or extending Continental/modern geometric methods are especially welcome; original speculations in these areas will be discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — transcendent calculus / analysis improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to the 'transcendent calculus, it is to be understood that whatever tends to the improvement of general processes, or the solution of important individual difficulties, will always receive particular attention and encouragement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept analyses that improve general analytical processes or solve notable specific problems; emphasis is on methodological advancement over mere numerical approximation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept applications to physical sciences and practical arts
rubrics_metrics.description: The application of mathematics to physical science and to the arts of life 'will always be welcomed by us,' and 'elementary illustrations of the manner of using general formule in special physical researches, will often be given' to help students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage submissions applying mathematics to military/civil engineering, architecture, navigation, practical astronomy, and other practical fields, especially when accompanied by elementary illustrations for student comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality relative to recent English and accessible French works
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editors 'shall, hence, generally lay down as a principle, that any real improvement upon the processes to be found in the most modern English, and the most generally accessible French works, is suitable for our pages, whether anticipated by other inquirers or not.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real improvements on recently published English and accessible French methods are acceptable even if similar work exists elsewhere; lack of absolute priority is not a bar provided the improvement is genuine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in number of questions and timing of answers
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors 'do not confine ourselves to any exact number of questions, or our correspondents to the time when they transmit their answers (leaving this to their own convenience)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No rigid quota of problems per issue and correspondents need not adhere to strict deadlines — submissions may be accepted on a flexible timetable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content categories accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Table of contents and editorial statements show acceptance of Algebra (transformations, equations, expansions), Plane and Solid Geometry (porisms, poles/polars, conic sections), Trigonometry, Probabilities, Calculus (variation of parameters, definite integrals), Miscellaneous mathematical notes, Solutions of exercises, and Collections of exercises for students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions across these classical mathematical areas are within scope, with the above qualitative selection preferences applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological preference — conditional coefficients and general instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors praise the 'method of conditional coefficients' as 'the true foundation of all transformation and of all development' and a general instrument for deriving many expansions and formulae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers explaining, applying, or advancing widely applicable methodological tools (e.g., conditional coefficients) are of interest; methodological clarity and demonstration of general applicability are valued.
